title: Capacity Sculptor: throughput SLAs, autoscale pattern insights, and right-sizing recommendations for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket scopes a new subsystem we’re calling Capacity Sculptor: a combined analysis + runtime recommendation engine that helps Dedicated customers meet throughput SLAs while minimizing cost. It will synthesize autoscaling policy patterns, historical throughput/latency signals, tenant packing heuristics, and KV-cache hit-rate insights to produce per-pool right-sizing suggestions and actionable autoscale policy recommendations.

Background / Motivation:
- Customers with Dedicated pools ask for: predictable throughput guarantees, lower monthly cost, and simpler autoscale policies. Today engineering teams manually tune pool sizes and scaling rules based on ad-hoc dashboards.
- We have existing telemetry tracked in console: per-route token rates, p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU utilization, request queue depth, cold-starts, and cache hit rates. However we lack a consolidated algorithmic layer to convert signals into safe downsize/upsize actions and policy templates.

Goals:
- Automatic, explainable right-sizing suggestions for Dedicated pools (scale-down candidates, headroom targets, packing recommendations).
- Autoscale policy pattern suggestions (min/max nodes, cooldowns, burst capacity knobs, proactive scale-outs around daily peaks).
- Ensure throughput SLAs are preserved: recommendations must include predicted SLA breach risk and mitigation plans (fallback models, temporary burst commit).
- UI surface in Console and an API endpoint for programmatic consumption.
- Measurement: reduce committed spend on eligible pools by >=10% in pilot without increasing SLA violations beyond baseline.

Signals & Metrics to Use:
- Per-tenant/time-series: requests/sec, tokens/sec, p50/p90/p99 latency, token tail-latency, GPU utilization, CPU/GPU memory percent, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, prefix reuse rate, autoscale event history, model variant fallbacks.
- Business KPIs: committed monthly spend, on-demand spend, SLA violations (count & duration), customer support tickets for throttling.

Proposed Architecture:
1) Offline analyzer (batch job) that ingests last 90 days of telemetry per Dedicated pool and computes: utilization distribution, peak cadence (hour-of-day/day-of-week heatmap), cold-start frequency, cache-hit-adjusted effective throughput, and churn. Output is a compact right-sizing profile + risk score.
2) Recommendation engine (microservice) that consumes the profile and generates: size suggestions (reserve X GPUs), autoscale template (min/max/cooldown/scale-step), and tenant packing hints (pack small tenants into shared pools, isolate tail-heavy tenants). Each recommendation has an explainability payload (which signals drove the suggestion).
3) Console integration: an interactive UI showing suggested action, projected cost delta, predicted SLA risk, and one-click apply (creates an internally gated change request for Dedicated pool managers).
4) Safe rollout: staged A/B evaluation where recommendations are first simulated (dry-run), then applied to non-critical pools with automated rollback if latency/SLA deviates.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Data pipeline: batch analyzer runs nightly and populates right-sizing profiles for >=80% of Dedicated pools with >7 days of telemetry.
- Recommendation quality: in pilot (20 pools) recommendations produce >=10% reduction in committed spend or on-demand usage without increasing SLA breach hours by more than 5% relative.
- Console UI: new 'Capacity Sculptor' panel exists with recommendation detail, cost delta, and an audit log entry on apply.
- API: /v1/dedicated/recommendations endpoint returns JSON recommendation + explainability fields.
- Tests: end-to-end tests for analyzer, recommendation engine, and a canary flow for apply/rollback.

Implementation Tasks (initial):
- T1: Define telemetry schema and selectors for analyzer (Mason).
- T2: Implement batch aggregator & heatmap generator (2 sprints).
- T3: Build recommendation rules engine (start with heuristic rules: headroom pct, peak cushion, cache-adjusted throughput).
- T4: Design explainability payload format and cost delta estimator (use current unit-cost model).
- T5: Console UI mockups and API design (work with PM/design).
- T6: Pilot pilot: identify 20 candidate pools and owners, run dry-run and then controlled apply.

Edge Cases & Constraints:
- Sparse telemetry pools (<24 hours) should be marked as insufficient data and receive conservative recommendations (no downsize).
- Customers with strict throughput guarantees (contractual SLA) must be opt-in for automated recommendations; default is advisory.
- Some pools host regulatory workloads—recommendations must honor isolation labels and RBAC.

Risk & Mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect downsize leads to SLA breach. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, simulated dry-run, and automatic rollback/alerting.
- Risk: noisy signals yield oscillation. Mitigation: require hysteresis and cooldown policies in suggested autoscale templates.
